title: Attorney General of Rhode Island

context.text: Incumbent Attorney General Peter Neronha is term-limited, so the seat is open. Kim Ahern won the September 9, 2026 Democratic primary and Alan Gordon is the Republican nominee.

candidates.name: Kim Ahern
candidates.currentRole: Chair, Rhode Island Cannabis Control Commission

priorities.text: Put the criminal prosecution unit front and center and prosecute violent offenders, while expanding diversion for people with mental illness and addiction.
Take the Trump administration to court when it oversteps its authority or threatens residents' rights.
Consumer protection, including price gouging, junk fees, utility rates (through the Public Utilities Commission) and health-care mergers.
Defend workers' right to organize and enforce prevailing wage and wage-theft laws.

positions.summary: Says she will defend Rhode Island's law codifying Roe v. Wade protections and use the office to protect access to reproductive health care.
positions.quote: As Attorney General, I will be ready to defend that law and ensure every Rhode Islander has the right to choose whether, how, and when to start a family.

statements.quote: That includes making sure Rhode Islanders understand their rights when approached by ICE or other federal law enforcement so no one is intimidated, targeted, or stripped of protections guaranteed under the law.

I will defend Rhode Island’s right to build clean energy infrastructure that helps address climate change while protecting shoreline access for Rhode Islanders and preserving the environment we cherish.

candidates.name: Alan Gordon
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the September 9, 2026 Republican primary. Ran for this office in 2018 as the Compassion Party nominee.
candidates.currentRole: Co-leader of The Healing Church (per NBC 10); not an attorney

priorities.text: Defend constitutional rights, protect vulnerable people, confront public corruption and apply "one standard of justice."
Review of the Department of Children, Youth and Families (DCYF) and Family Court, listed on his campaign site.

positions.summary: Opposes Rhode Island's bans on assault weapons and large-capacity magazines, telling NBC 10 that they appear to be incursions on the right to bear arms.
positions.quote: They seem to me to be obvious incursions into the right to bear arms that really the courts are going to have to take a look at

statements.quote: The laws, whether I like them or not, are the laws of Rhode Island. They protect that terrible choice.
statements.context: To NBC 10 News; he describes himself as anti-abortion and said he would not seek to change the state's law

record.text: Arrested October 4, 2018 with Compassion Party gubernatorial nominee Anne Armstrong at their West Greenwich home after state police reported finding 48 pounds of marijuana. Fox News reported they appeared in court the same day and did not enter pleas on charges of marijuana possession and contributing to the delinquency of a minor (a 15-year-old was in the home), and were held on $25,000 bail. NBC 10 reported in October 2026 that he was not convicted in that case or in a 2016 arrest; Gordon says all charges were dismissed. The final court disposition was not found in a court record.

researchNotes: Slate: Rhode Island's official certified list for the general election could not be located on elections.ri.gov (the Secretary of State's candidate pages return 403); the two-candidate slate rests on Rhode Island Current's Nov. 3 voter guide, NBC 10 (Oct 16, 2026) and Ballotpedia, and a Providence Eye forum report. No independent AG candidate was found. Ahern holds a state post (Cannabis Control Commission chair) but no commission votes were reviewed. Gordon's 2018 arrest is stated per rule 9 from Fox News and NBC 10 reports I fetched; the Providence Journal articles were paywalled.
